newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hindu party rebels form state government.
newsitem.headline: India Hindu party rebels form state government.

text.p: India's western state of Gujarat had a new government on Wednesday after breakaway lawmakers of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India's main opposition party, took office.
The new administration marks the end of New Delhi's direct rule of the state, a step also officially approved by the nation's president on Wednesday.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Shankarsinh Vaghela, leader of the newly formed Mahagujarat Janata Party (MJP) which split from the Hindu-nationalist BJP in August, was sworn in at a ceremony in the state capital of Gandhinagar.
The new government has been formed with support from former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's Congress party, the BJP's arch-foe.
The MJP has 50 members and Congress 44 in the 181-seat state assembly, giving them a paper majority.
Gujarat was brought under direct rule last month after the BJP, the single largest party in the federal parliament, split into two there, forcing the fall of the state government.
Earlier on Wednesday, Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma revoked New Delhi's direct rule in the state.

The formation of a non-BJP government in Gujarat is seen as a setback to the party, which is trying to recapture power in New Delhi after briefly forming a minority administration earlier this year after inconclusive general elections.
Earlier this month, the BJP suffered a blow during elections to the state assembly of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state.
The BJP won 177 seats in the 425-seat assembly, belying pre-poll predictions of a wider lead.
